title: Open-closed recollement
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a
closed immersion with
complementary
open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative
ring. For every $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ there is a functorial
distinguished triangle

$$
j_!j^{-1}K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow i_*i^{-1}K
\longrightarrow j_!j^{-1}K[1],
$$

where $i_*$ is the (exact) direct image of the closed immersion, and
the first two arrows are respectively the counit and unit of the adjunctions
$j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$ on the small etale sites, induced on derived categories by the exact functors. Here $j_!$ is [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], inverse image is [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and direct image is [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Functorial means that every morphism $K\to K'$ induces a morphism of these triangles with the three indicated functorial components, including the square involving the connecting map.

proof.text: Use the four exact sheaf functors and their levelwise functors on D⁺. The closed immersion is finite, so its direct image is exact; inverse image and extension by zero have the exactness instances already used in the theorem signature. The source mapDerivedCategoryPlusAdjunction restricts the levelwise derived adjunction, with its specified unit and counit, along the fully faithful inclusion D⁺ → D. The open sheaf unit and closed sheaf counit are isomorphisms. Their levelwise derived versions are isomorphisms, as are their restrictions to D⁺.

The sheaf vanishings i^* j_! = 0 and j^* i_* = 0 pass to D⁺: exact functors commute with every homology object, so the composite levelwise derived functor has zero homology in every degree. The fully faithful inclusion of D⁺ reflects zero objects.

The sheaf short exact sequence is natural: a sheaf map f supplies the three components j_! j^* f, f, i_* i^* f, and the two squares are naturality of the counit and unit. If j^* f and i^* f are invertible, both outer components are invertible. The short five lemma therefore makes f invertible. Since exact functors commute with homology, the same joint reflection of isomorphisms holds on D, hence on D⁺. This uses the unit’s own sheaf short exact sequence; no independent conservativity assumption is introduced.

Write J=j^*, L=j_!, I=i^*, R=i_* for the exact functors on D⁺. Complete the open counit L J K → K to a distinguished triangle L J K → K →[g] C → L J K[1]. Applying J makes the first arrow invertible by the open triangle identity and invertible unit, hence J C=0. Applying I kills the first object by step 2, hence I g is invertible. The unit C → R I C becomes invertible after J (both sides vanish by step 2) and after I (it is inverse to the invertible closed counit). Step 3 makes that unit invertible. Thus e:C ≅ R I K is the unit at C followed by R((I g)⁻¹). Naturality and cancellation give g ≫ e.hom = unit_K. Transport the cone triangle along the identity on its first two objects and e on its third object. Its first two arrows are exactly the required counit and unit.

Choose the connecting maps from step 4. For K,K′, the closed adjunction identifies Hom((L J K)[1], R I K′) with Hom(I((L J K)[1]), I K′); the source of the latter is zero by step 2 and shift compatibility. Consequently this Hom is a singleton. Apply the triangle-morphism extension theorem to f:K → K′ and the prescribed components L J f and R I f. Their first two squares are counit and unit naturality. The extension theorem supplies the third square with exactly these components, namely R I f ≫ δ(K′) = δ(K) ≫ (L J f)[1]. This proves functoriality for every derived morphism directly.
